predecessors.name: Kingdom of England
predecessors.text: Maurice FitzGerald's Desmond lands, which the Crown made an earldom in 1329 and confirmed as the county palatine of Kerry

successors.name: Kingdom of England
successors.text: the Desmond estates 'forfeit to the English Crown' in 1583 and planted with English colonists after a survey begun in 1584

ledger.x: 1329: Edward III makes Maurice FitzGerald Earl of Desmond (27 August).
1331: the Crown takes Dunamark, at the head of Bantry Bay.
1579: the Earl joins the Second Desmond Rebellion by sacking Youghal (13 November).
1583: the Earl is hunted down and killed.

wars.name: Desmond's revolt of 1345
wars.outcome: The 1st Earl presided at an assembly at Callan in 1345, ignored a summons, attacked Nenagh, surrendered on a promise of his life, was imprisoned and lost his lands; released in 1348 and pardoned in 1349.

wars.name: Desmond-Thomond war of 1370
wars.outcome: 'In 1370 Brian O'Brien of Thomond expelled his cousin Turlough.

wars.name: First Desmond Rebellion
wars.outcome: English victory: James FitzMaurice attacked the English colony at Kerrycurihy in June 1569, Donal MacCarthy Mor surrendered in November 1569, and FitzMaurice submitted on 23 February 1573.

wars.name: Second Desmond Rebellion
wars.outcome: English victory: Smerwick 18 July 1579, Youghal sacked 13 November 1579, papal troops landed at Smerwick 10 September 1580, the rebellion crushed by mid-1581, the Earl killed in November 1583; the estates are forfeit and planted.

certainty.note: A feudal earldom with no survey: the page describes its land only as 'historically' Limerick, Cork, Kerry and Waterford, and the western part was a semi-independent Gaelic kingdom to 1596.
